title: Technology picker: AI Development Algorithm and Psychoarchaeology
description: The picker's own prerequisite check knew nothing of AI Development Algorithm or Psychoarchaeology (rules version 15), so it dimmed unit upgrades the engine offers and refused exhausted specialty planets that Psychoarchaeology makes usable. Now a first pick trusts the engine's list (version 15+), the second pick and the track arithmetic model aida (ready card, unit upgrades, spent last, not after the first pick spent it) and The Prophet's Tears, cards say when aida is what unlocks them, and exhausted specialty planets can be toggled under Psychoarchaeology. Before shots are taken on 0a18dd87 (TI4_SHOT_PREFIX=before); after shots are regenerated by npm run screenshots -- FX. Synthetic tables through a mocked server, with the option lists the engine produces for those tables (checked by the shared parity table).

notes.title: Root cause
notes.text: TechnologyModal ANDed the engine's option list with its own checkTechPrerequisites (owned track counts, toggled ready planets, a Jol-Nar budget). Anything the engine knows beyond that (aida's ignore-1 on unit upgrades, Psychoarchaeology's free exhausted specialties) made a legal option look unavailable, and exhausted planets were never offered for toggling.

notes.title: Scenarios
notes.text: aida-unlocks: Sol owns AI Development Algorithm, Antimass Deflectors and Sarween Tools; Cruiser II (G Y R) and Dreadnought II (B B Y) are each one short and the engine lists them. aida-exhausted: Same table, the card is exhausted: the engine does not list Cruiser II or Dreadnought II. pa-exhausted-planet: Sol owns Psychoarchaeology and controls Thibah (blue specialty), exhausted. The engine lists Gravity Drive (B). plain: Sol owns Antimass Deflectors and Sarween Tools only.

notes.title: Parity
notes.text: crates/ti4-engine/testdata/tech_waiver_parity.json is read by the engine test tech_picker_parity_table_matches_can_research (asserts can_research) and by web/src/presentation/technologyWaivers.test.ts (asserts the client check): 19 scenarios, both agree.

notes.title: Not modelled client-side
notes.text: Research Team laws and Publicize Weapon Schematics: the client has no data for them, so the first pick relies on the engine's list and the second pick's own check does not count them. Jol-Nar's budget is untouched (its literal 'unit_upgrade' test never matched the catalog's UNITUPGRADE, so it has always been 2 for every technology).
